lessons.title: 1. Modern JavaScript Variables & Functions
lessons.description: An arrow function expression has a shorter syntax compared to function expressions. Implement `calculateTotal(price, tax)` as a `const` arrow function returning `price + price * tax`, and export it with `module.exports = { calculateTotal }`. The tests check calculateTotal(100, 0.1) === 110 and calculateTotal(50, 0.2) === 60.
lessons.solution_code:
const calculateTotal = (price, tax) => price + (price * tax);
module.exports = { calculateTotal };

tests.name: test_calculate_total

exercises.question: Which keyword defines block-scoped variables that cannot be reassigned?
exercises.explanation: const is block-scoped and cannot be reassigned; let can be.

learning_objectives: Declare constants with const (block-scoped, no reassignment)
Write arrow functions as compact expressions

source.name: MDN Web Docs — Functions guide — 'An arrow function expression has a shorter syntax compared to function expressions'

lessons.title: 5. Mapping Over Arrays
lessons.description: Array.prototype.map() returns a new array containing the results of invoking a function on every element in the calling array. Implement doubleAll(numbers) as an arrow function returning a new array with every value doubled via map, exported with module.exports. The test checks doubleAll([1, 2, 3]) produces [2, 4, 6].
learning_objectives: Transform every array element with map()
Understand that map returns a NEW array
Compose arrow functions with built-in array methods

source.name: MDN Web Docs — GlobalObjects — Array.prototype.map(): 'Returns a new array containing the results of invoking a function on every element'

lessons.solution_code:
const doubleAll = (numbers) => numbers.map((n) => n * 2);
module.exports = { doubleAll };

tests.name: test_double_all

exercises.question: What does `numbers.map(double)` return?
options: the original array, changed in place
a brand new array holding each transformed value
undefined, because the callback has no return value
exercises.correct_answer: a brand new array holding each transformed value
exercises.explanation: `map` never mutates its receiver: it builds and returns a new array of the callback's results.
